answer.evidence: This is a face-on display shelf, not an open container. Rows 1-7 are a flat header strip with stripes. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no receding plane, so it is a vertical cornice or sign band. Below it, rows 8-27 are shelves of onigiri and bento boxes drawn face-on, with horizontal shelf lines at about rows 14-15 and 21-22. Rows 28-30 are a plain base strip. No ellipse, rim or visible opening contents are drawn, and the silhouette is a full-width rectangle of 46 px on every row. Nothing shows a horizontal surface seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a front-on shelf unit with a thin striped awning, pale shelf frame and rows of tiny coloured product dots. The measured facts are mixed. Visible tones per tile (16) match prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20), and near-flat coverage is 0%, so the product dots do give some texture. But 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and cheese stall and 33-44% for the well and bench, so the neutral dark outline reads as a uniform sticker line. The frame and body, which are the main material, show only about 3 lightness steps (white, light grey, dark line) with no per-material shading, grain or form modelling. The references use 5-6 steps with tinted material-tone edges. The tone count comes mostly from the small product dots, not from shaded materials. A careful artist would find it flatter and more sticker-like beside the cheese stall and the well, so it fails on outline and shading depth despite adequate tone count.
